It features a unique blend of set collection and card drafting with the approachable feel of a roll-and-write game. Draft locations from across the European continent as you collect sets of activities and try delicious food to gain the most points. Boomerang: Europe is a stand-alone game in the Boomerang family that plays similarly to the original Boomerang, but has some rules differences and new ways to score. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Gameplay 2 Scoring 3 End of the Game 4 Variants Gameplay The game consists of 4 rounds. At the start of each round, deal 7 cards to each player. The others are not used for the round. On your turn, pick a card you want, then pass the rest to the left. All cards drafted are not revealed. After 7 turns, all hands are depleted and drafted cards are scored. Afterwards, shuffle all 28 cards and start a new round. Scoring Throw and Catch: The first card drafted in a round is the throw, and the last card drafted is the catch. Score points equal to the absolute difference between them. Tourist Sites: Cross out all countries visited each round. At the end of the game, each visited country is worth 1 point. The first player to visit all countries in a region scores 2-5 points. Passport Bonus: If you have visited at least one country in each region, score 7/3/1 points. Cuisine: Total all scores on icons. If the sum is larger than 7, score half of the total. Otherwise, score normally. Transport: For each pair of transport scores the points marked. National Treasures: Choose an unscored treasure that you have at least one of. Score 4/3/2 points (for 2/3/4 players) for each matching treasure drafted by an opponent. End of the Game The game ends after 4 rounds. The player with the highest score wins. If there is a tie, the player with the highest throw and catch wins. Variants Direction Variant: Alternate passing to the left and to the right each round. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] A game with geography theme where a lot of countries are mislabeled!? Is this game a joke?

[Rating: 2/10] I remain someone who doesn't really enjoy pick-and-pass card drafting, and whilst this might be an actually-simple implementation of that mechanism unlike often-recommended titles like 7 Wonders, I still didn't find it to be something engaging. (I've also played the Australia version and find this much the same; I don't think I prefer one of them in particular.)

[Rating: 3/10] Doesn't ticks the boxes for a good roll/write for me. I guess it is the combination with the drafting.

[Rating: 3/10] Decent little drafting game, but the writing part of it feels tacked on. It also seems relatively unbalanced towards certain scoring types. Not sure I need or want to play this.

[Rating: 4/10] An attempt to establish draft-and-write? Basic drafting and set collection game with an unnecessary "write" part. Also kind of a point salad with everything scoring for something. Playable but unremarkable.

[Rating: 4/10] Draft and write, point salad-y thing. I'm already hard pressed to enjoy games in this genre anyway, but the point salad nature of the cards means that there isn't really hate drafting or anything, which just turns it into a pile of pick a thing and whatever. I don't know. It does seem like people like this, and so I guess I just need to assume it isn't for me, and is for someone who wants a more relaxed drafting experience.

[Rating: 4.5/10] I like it. It's not great, and I'm worried about how long it will stay interesting for, but it's enjoyable for now.

[Rating: 5/10] I'm someone who puts theme first. And then this game is very disappointing. Norway is neither known for their beer, nor for its architecture. (Ok, stave curches FTW!) Things like that were criticized (during the KS?) and the publisher responded they put balance over theme. Well, get both right, pls. In this regard, the "transport" icons were also disappointing. Cool: This country has... cars. It could have been activities. Would have been cool. Misprinted sheets didn't make that better.

[Rating: 5/10] I love Boomerang Australia but the small differences in scoring for this version makes me rate this one much lower.

[Rating: 5/10] 2021-01-10 - 5 - a fine drafting game but worse than it's predecessor, which is more interesting and has more depth. And this version has 8 country cards not matching the right countries on the notebook. France points to Portugal, Norway points to Denmark and so on. That's a shame and a big omission by Matagot, which is the European publisher of this game. Unfortunately that's a missed opportunity to make a great reedition of the great game.

[Rating: 5/10] Grecja to wysepka na Morzu Jońskim (Malta), Francja to Portugalia, a Portugalia to Francja. Dania leży tam gdzie Finlandia, Finlandia tam gdzie Szwecja, Szwecja tam gdzie Norwegia. A Norwegia gdzie? Norwegia tam gdzie Dania. Malta? Malta graniczy z Albanią i Macedonią, bo jest Grecją.  Nie wiem czy to jest świadomy żart ze znajomości geografii Europy przez Amerykanów czy to jakieś upośledzenie autora/wydawnictwa ale wyszło epicko.

[Rating: 5/10] Definitely my least favorite of the revised Boomerang games - the national treasure scoring is a large part of this because it's just much too easy to score 8-10 points every round. I am told this works better with fewer players, but with four I would always play Australia or USA.  ETA: Having played with three, I can say that a)it does work a bit better that way but b)I still prefer Australia and USA. For one thing, I still don't like the national treasure scoring that much. For another, aside from that issue I prefer playing these games with four because all the cards are dealt.

[Rating: 5/10] Designer: Scott Almes Playing time:  15-30 Min Weight: 2.00 / 5  Publisher: Matagot  [b]COMPLEXITY:[/b] Medium. The rules are simple - is a draft game, much simpler than 7 Wonders, as there is no consideration about demands to take cards. Is more akin to Fairy Tale and Sushi Go, as the only thing that matters is to pick cards to make the most points. Now, about points, the meeting during design of the game surely went this way: Publisher: So, how many things to score do you want? Designer: Yes. There are about 1 million ways to score points in the game. Basically every card you pick will score

[Rating: 5/10] Pick-and-pass card game that's worth a few plays. Not really enough here to last beyond that.

[Rating: 5/10] Seems complicated for such a simple game. Too much for too little. draft and write seems like unnecesary and makes game tedious to write everything down, yet you just drafted only 7 cards, now to write all of them down, nah not streamlined enough for me.

[Rating: 5/10] Of all the Boomerangs, this is my favourite in the way things are getting scored. I love x-and-write games. This one is okay. Quite original to see a draft-and-write but not a game I am quite excited about playing.

[Rating: 5/10] Nem igazán győzött meg. Jópofa a térkép és az, hogy az európai országokat utazgatva próbálunk GYP-ot adó sorozatokat, ikonokat gyűjtögetni, de önmagába véve a játék motorja épp, hogy elégséges. Sok szerencse, és ráadásul esetlenül. Ha nem lenne ez a jópofa "európai országok" máz nem érne semmit ez a játék. Nem is az a baj, hogy nagyon primitívek a játék által támasztott feladatok, hanem, hogy semmi igazi csavar nincs a játékban. Egyszerűen fantáziátlan a mechanika.
